sentences.text: The appellants/claimants - wife, children and mother of the deceased Nagappa - are before this Court in this appeal not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under the judgment and award, dated 31.10.2015, passed in M.V.C. No.272/2014 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Haveri (for short, 'the Tribunal') and praying for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Haveri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case leading to filing of this appeal are that,
(a) The appellants/claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, seeking compensation for the accidental death of Nagappa in a road traffic accident that took place on 09.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 27/R-3358 and NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-27/F-538.

They claimed that the deceased was an agriculturist earning more than Rs.15,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB per month, and aged 42 years as on the date of the accident.

(b) On issuance of notice, the respondent-North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (for short, 'the Corporation') appeared and filed its objections contending that the claim is exorbitant and excessive.

entities.text: North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It further contended that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself.
It also contended that the deceased was not having a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
Thus, it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
(c) In support of their case, the claimants examined claimant No.1, the wife of the deceased, as P.W.1 apart from marking 18 documents as Exs.P1 to P18.
On behalf of the respondent, conductor of the offending bus was examined as R.W.1.
No document was produced by the respondent in support of its case.
Based on the material on record, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.7,96,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit of compensation amount.

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, adopted multiplier '14', and deducted 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The Tribunal failed to award any compensation on the head 'future prospects' and also towards loss of consortium to the claimants.
The claimants, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded, are before this Court in this appeal.

3. A perusal of the judgment and award of the Tribunal would indicate that the Tribunal failed to award any compensation on the head 'future prospects' which the claimants would be entitled to at Smt.Shaila vs The Divisional Manager on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139447299/
3 25% of the assessed income since the deceased was aged 45 years as on the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7801-DB date of the accident.

entities.text: Smt.Shaila vs The Divisional Manager on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, it is seen that the Tribunal has failed to award Rs.40,000/- each to the claimants who are wife, children and mother of the deceased on the head of 'loss of spousal, parental and filial consortium'.

4. Sri. C.B.Patil, learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation would support the judgment passed by the Tribunal and would submit that the Tribunal has awarded just compensation which needs no interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation and on perusal of the appeal papers including the records of the Tribunal, the only point that falls for consideration in this appeal is, Whether the appellants-claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?
6.
The answer to the above point would be in affirmative for the following reasons.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB (a) The accident that took place on 09.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-27/R-3358 and NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-27/F- 538 and the resultant death of Nagappa, the husband of claimant No.1, is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimants are in this appeal praying for enhancement of compensation.
Moreover, the respondent- Corporation has not filed any appeal.
(b) The accident is of the year 2014.
It is stated that the deceased was doing agricultural work earning more than Rs.15,000/- per month.

To establish the income and avocation of the deceased,
the claimants have not produced any material.
In the absence of any material to establish the income, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income of the deceased notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2014 is Rs.7,500/- per month.

In the absence of any material being produced to establish the income of the deceased, it would be appropriate to assess the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month and hence, the monthly income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.7,500/-.

Admittedly, the deceased was aged 45 years and, in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1, the claimants would be entitled to adding 25% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects'.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to addition of 25% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects'.

(c) The multiplier '14' adopted by the Tribunal, and deduction of 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased is proper and correct.
(d) Since the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.7,500/-, the compensation, which the claimants would be entitled to, under the head 'loss of dependency' would be in a sum of Rs.11,81,250/- AIR 2017 SC 5157 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB [Rs.7,500/- + Rs.1,875/- (25%) =
Rs.9,375/- less Rs.2,343.75 (1/4th of Rs.9,375) = Rs.7,031.25 x 12 x 14].
Smt.Shaila vs The Divisional Manager on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139447299/
4

(e) The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the heads of 'loss of consortium',
'loss of love and affection', 'loss of estate', and towards 'funeral expenses and transportation'.

However, in view of the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others and Pranay Sethi's case (supra), the claimants - wife, children and mother of the deceased - would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each on the head of 'loss of spousal, parental and filial consortium'.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the heads 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.

7. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
2018 ACJ 2782 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB 1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 11,81,250/-
2) Loss of spousal, parental and filial Rs. 2,00,000/-
 consortium (to claimants No.1 to  5) (Rs.40,000 x 5)
 3) Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 4) Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
TOTAL Rs

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,11,250/- as against Rs.7,96,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

8. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The above appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,11,250/- as against Rs.7,96,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

d) The respondent-NWKRTC shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7801-DB from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
